home.seoDesc: Build a wishlist and share it with one link. For gifts, birthdays and weddings: friends open the link to browse, then sign in to pledge a gift. No duplicates, no overselling.
home.ogDesc: List what you want, so the people who want to give never have to guess.
home.lead: List what you want, so the people who want to give never have to guess.
home.sub: Share your whole wishlist with one link. Friends open it to browse, then sign in to pledge a gift. No duplicates, no overselling.
home.demoAria: Example wishlist: three items, one already pledged
home.scenesTitle: Three occasions, one kind of list

gift.d: The recipient makes the list and givers pick from it. No more guessing sizes, colors or tastes.

birthday.t: One link gathers all the love
birthday.d: Just paste it in the group chat. Everyone picks one item, or chips in together for a big gift.

wedding.t: Set up the new home in one go
wedding.d: List appliances, tableware and household goods. Once a guest pledges an item, it is locked right away.

origin: The person who needs something can’t bring themselves to ask, and the person who wants to give has no idea what’s missing. So everyone buys the same baby bottle and nobody buys the formula.
Gifting and donating share one problem: supply and demand are out of sync.
That’s why I built Wishly: list what you want, share one link, and let people claim items without ever over-claiming, so the one who needs and the one who gives finally line up.
home.stepsTitle: Share your wishes in three steps

1.d: Add the items you want with prices and links. Ten minutes is enough.

2.d: Send it through LINE, Facebook or anywhere else. The preview image comes along automatically.

3.d: Open the link to look around. Sign in to pledge an item, and nobody else can pick it afterwards.

0.d: Each item can be pledged by only one person, even if two people tap at the same moment.

1.d: Friends can view a list without an account, and sign in only when they want to pledge.

2.d: Pledges and progress sync instantly. No need to refresh the page.

3.d: Big items can be funded by several people, and the progress bar shows what is still missing.

0.q: Do my friends need to sign up?
0.a: Not to browse a list. To pledge an item they need to sign in first.

1.q: Could two people give the same item?
1.a: No. Once an item is pledged it is locked, and pledges that are not completed in time are released automatically.

2.q: Can I show a list only to certain people?
2.a: Yes. A list can be public, visible to all friends, visible to close friends only, or private to you.
